verdict.rationale: Both refactors split `process_order` into the same pipeline of steps, and both preserve behavior, including releasing `order.items` on a declined payment, which is equivalent to the old reserved list. B's pinned tests are stronger: they check the exact boundaries (4999 and 5000), per-line tax rounding versus summed, the full stock-operation log on a decline, log records, and the ordering of the receipt send. B also checked its tests with a mutation script. A has a better process: it added tests to the existing file and asked before committing, while B committed to local main unasked and duplicated test helpers in a new file.
a_issues: The 'just below 5000' shipping test actually uses 4500, so it does not pin the real boundary.
The coupon-not-redeemed test relies on an obscure trick: it calls `redeem()` and then asserts the coupon still has uses.
`_discount` mixes coupon lookup and validation (it can raise) with the arithmetic.
b_issues: Committed twice to local main without being asked.
The new test file duplicates `make_order` and `CUSTOMER` from `test_checkout.py`, and some test lines are very long.
The report has a garbled sentence ('the mutation tools  mentions aren't installed').

verdict.rationale: Both refactors split process_order into almost the same steps and both preserve behavior. Each also makes the same safe change of releasing order.items on a declined payment. A's characterization tests are stronger: they cover the exact 4999/5000 shipping boundary, per-line rounding that differs from summed rounding, exact log records and the call order of the receipt. A also keeps _discount pure by moving the coupon lookup into _coupon_percent. B's change is just as correct but its tests pin less, and A's reported mutation check adds confidence.
a_issues: Committed twice to local main without being asked.
The report has a garbled phrase ("the mutation tools  mentions aren't installed").
Characterization tests go in a new separate file instead of the existing test_checkout.py.
b_issues: The shipping test named 'just below 5000' uses 4500, not 4999, so it does not pin the exact boundary.
The failed-receipt test checks only the log text, not the log level or traceback; the zero-quantity test does not check that the status is unchanged.
_discount both looks up the coupon (and can raise OrderRejected) and computes the discount, which is less cleanly separated than A's split.
